observations: A roughly circular head form fills most of the canvas against a dark grey ground, with spiky black marks radiating outward along the top and sides.
The left eye area contains a tight inward spiral of blue and yellow lines nested inside a square-cornered outline; the right side shows overlapping triangular red and white lines on a pink field.
The lower third is dominated by a tooth-filled mouth showing a row of grey-white rectangular teeth, outlined and cross-hatched in black, with red and yellow scribbled lines running beneath the jaw.
reading: The face pushes to the edges of the frame, its two eye zones built from opposite geometries — a coiling spiral on the left, a jagged triangular tangle on the right. That asymmetry reads as unease rather than balance. The bared teeth below carry enough solidity to feel like a fixed state rather than a passing expression. Loose marks at the crown and sides keep the whole form from settling.
contextAngle: Within the owned nnotb subset, title neighbors #208 and #210 share the same dark ground and bared-teeth mouth. #209 is the most saturated of the three, with pink and yellow pushing against the dark field more forcefully than in either neighbor.

connections.reason: Both works place a circular head on a near-identical dark teal-grey ground with a yellow diagonal mark in the upper left, but #208 keeps its palette darker and murkier where #209 breaks into bright pink and open white.

Both #209 and #210 feature a prominent spiral eye and a row of white teeth on the same dark ground, but #210 places the spiral on the right and uses tighter concentric rings, reversing the lateral emphasis.

lookingQuestion: How does the difference in geometry between the left eye's inward spiral and the right eye's triangular lines affect the way you move across the face?
ambiguities: The square outline around the left spiral eye could be a structural element of the face or a separate overlaid shape; the image does not resolve this.
